decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach toward the yellow bottle, using small increments from the initial configuration; right arm remains clear.
Advance left open gripper toward the standing yellow bottle, above the lying bottle, while leveling the wrist.
Reduce approach increments after continuity rejection; maintain the existing elbow-up branch and clearance.
Move the open left fingers toward the yellow bottle at upper-body height, avoiding the lying bottle below.
Align left fingers around the yellow bottle's body with a slow forward and downward approach; keep open until alignment is visible.
Close the left gripper on the yellow bottle, then lift vertically to check retention and clear the table.
Yellow bottle appears retained above the table. Carry it left toward the bin with the gripper commanded closed.
Continue carrying the retained yellow bottle over the left bin, preserving elbow-up continuity and keeping closed.
Open above the bin to release the yellow bottle, then withdraw gently; check the images for the drop before approaching the next bottle.
The yellow bottle has dropped into the bin. Move left above the lying bottle and gradually orient the open fingers for a top-down grasp.
Continue the elevated left approach and gradual top-down rotation toward the lying bottle's narrow shoulder, keeping the other arm stationary.
Bring the left wrist over the lying bottle while completing the downward approach orientation. Keep clearance and fingers open.
Lower slowly toward the lying bottle's shoulder, correcting finger alignment for a downward grasp; inspect before closing.
Descent showed contact or tracking resistance. Reposition slightly toward the bottle's narrower neck and correct orientation before attempting closure.
Try closing at the neck without further downward pressure, then make a short vertical lift to test visual retention.
Lift a little farther with the left gripper closed to determine whether the lying bottle is retained at the neck.
The bottle remained on the table. Reopen and shift the downward grasp toward the neck center, aligning across the bottle before another slow descent.
The neck is now centered between the open fingers. Descend a short distance and close without further downward motion.
Keep the left gripper closed and lift vertically to verify that the bottle follows the neck grasp.
The bottle now follows the left hand. Carry it leftward above the table with the neck grasp closed, maintaining the current elbow-up configuration.
Continue moving the retained bottle over the bin; keep the bottle horizontal and the left fingers closed.
Release the pale bottle over the bin and withdraw the left hand. Begin a small, elbow-up right-arm approach to the pink bottle.
Approach the pink bottle with the right hand while moving the left hand to a separate central receiving posture; rotate gradually and keep both grippers open.
Advance the right open fingers toward the pink bottle's body. Continue preparing the left receiving hand on its own side of the centerline.
Align the right fingers around the pink bottle's middle while the left hand waits open in a separate receiving position.
Reduce left wrist rotation after the continuity guard. Continue the slow right approach without closing until the bottle is centered.
Close the right gripper around the pink bottle and lift slightly to confirm retention; the left hand waits open.
The pink bottle follows the right hand. Move it toward the central handover area, below and clear of the open left fingers.
Bring the pink bottle into the open left fingers for an upper-body handover, keeping the right grasp closed and the wrists vertically separated.
Close the left fingers on the upper pink bottle while the right hand continues supporting it; do not release the donor yet.
The handover did not show secure retention. Reopen and withdraw the left hand, and slightly lift the right to locate the pink bottle before retrying.
Separate the open right hand from the bottle to inspect its location after the uncertain handover. Keep the left arm clear and stationary.
Both remaining bottles are on the table. Clear the right hand and begin orienting the left hand above the white bottle for a downward recovery grasp.
Continue the elevated left approach toward the white bottle, rotating gradually for a grasp across its body; keep the right arm clear.
Align the left gripper downward across the lying white bottle and approach from above, keeping the right hand stationary and clear.
Make a short, slow downward alignment over the white bottle's body while leaving the fingers open.
Close on the white bottle and lift a short distance to test whether it is securely retained.
Lift and move the white bottle slightly left with the gripper closed, checking that it follows before carrying it to the bin.
White bottle remained on the table. Reopen and recenter the downward grasp over its body using the current head view.
Fine-center the white bottle between the fingers, lower a small amount, and close while stationary.
Lift the white bottle vertically with the left fingers closed, verifying retention before transport.
The white bottle did not follow the lift. Reopen and approach lower around its body, monitoring clearance rather than assuming a grasp.
Fine-center and lower the open left fingers around the white bottle, then close while stationary.
Lift the closed left grasp vertically, checking that the white bottle remains between the fingers and clears the table.
The white bottle now follows the lift. Carry it left above the table with the fingers closed and the wrist orientation unchanged.
Continue carrying the visibly retained white bottle toward the left bin, keeping the gripper closed.
Move the white bottle fully over the bin and release. Begin a gradual right-hand overhead approach to recover the lying pink bottle.
The white bottle has dropped into the bin. Advance the right hand above the pink bottle while withdrawing and leveling the left hand.
Rotate the right fingers downward across the pink bottle and align above its body. Keep the left arm separated and open.
Lower the right open fingers around the pink bottle's body while positioning the left hand clear for a later transfer.
Close the right grasp around the pink bottle and lift slightly to check retention before attempting another transfer.
Lift the retained pink bottle toward the central transfer area; turn the open left fingers for a side grasp on a separate part of the horizontal bottle.
Bring the donor right wrist toward the center without crossing it. Lower and roll the open left hand while maintaining clearance for a separate-body grasp.
Hold the pink bottle steady in the right hand. Align the left open fingers above and below the free lower portion for a side handover.
Slide the open left fingers around the free end of the horizontal pink bottle while the right hand holds it steady.
Shift the left grip slightly inward from the bottle's base and close on the free body section. Keep the right donor closed until retention is checked.
Keep the left receiving grasp closed, open the right donor, and withdraw it slightly to check whether the pink bottle remains with the left hand.
The pink bottle appears supported by the left hand after donor release. Carry it left and upward while withdrawing the open right arm on its own side.
Continue carrying the retained pink bottle toward the bin, gradually turning it within the left workspace. Return the open right hand toward its home side.
Move the pink bottle fully over the bin and turn its length toward the opening. Keep it closed until its clearance is visible; continue the right-arm return.
Release the pink bottle above the bin, then gently withdraw the left hand. Bring the open right arm close to its origin while preserving continuity.
The pink bottle has dropped into the bin. Return both open hands toward their origins, using small right-arm increments near home and gradually unrolling the left wrist.
Continue the open left-arm return with gradual wrist leveling, and settle the right hand at its origin.
Finish the left-arm return to origin with decreasing increments and both grippers open, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
